paragraphs: Qodem sheyyebarek veyitattep yekavven leqayyem mitzvat aseh lilbosh tzitzit metzuyyetzet kehilkato shenneemar veasu lahem tzitzit al kanpe bigdehem vehi mitzvat aseh shehazzeman gerama, veal yede kavvanat hakana zo az yihyeh koach bahakanato bibraka lehaalot mayin nuqbin ulehamshik hammochin kemo shekkatab rabbenu harasha"sh binhar shalom, velaken tob lomar bepiv qodem habberaka: "leshem yichud qudesha berik hu ushekinatah veku' hareni mukan lilbosh tzitzit metzuyyetzet kahalaka kemo shetztzivvanu Adonai elohenu veasu lahem tzitzit al kanpe bigdehem kede laasot nachat rucha leyotzerenu veku'", vegam tzarik lekavven beet shemmitattep bo shetztzivvanu haqqadosh-baruk-hu lehitattep bo kede shennizkor kol mitzotayv laasotam, vekatebu haacharonim za"l mi sheeno oseh kak alayv neemar vattehi yiratam oti mitzvat anashim melummada:

clarification.explanation: Before reciting the blessing over the tzitzit and wrapping oneself in it, one must have in mind that he is fulfilling a positive Torah commandment — to wear valid tzitzit, as it is said, "and they shall make for themselves tzitzit on the corners of their garments." This is a time-bound commandment. This intention gives special power to the blessing, and therefore it is good to say, before the blessing, the wording of "for the sake of the unification" which expresses the preparation and intention to fulfill the commandment properly, in order to give satisfaction to the Creator. In addition, at the time of the actual wrapping, one must have in mind that the Holy One, blessed be He, commanded us to wrap ourselves in tzitzit so that we remember all the commandments and fulfill them. One who does not do so is considered to be fulfilling the commandment merely out of habit, without the intention of the heart.
takeaways: Before the blessing and the wrapping, one should consciously intend that he is fulfilling the positive commandment of tzitzit, and recite "for the sake of the unification" in order to strengthen the intention.
At the time of the wrapping itself, one should intend that the purpose is to remember all the commandments, and not perform the commandment merely out of habit.

paragraphs: Yebarek lehitattep betzitzit bshb" tachat be"t velo bepata"ch, vetzarik lekavven bebirkat hattallit gadol liptor tallit qatan shealayv shello pashetu ballayla, mishshum deikka disbira lehu shetztzarik lebarek al tallit qatan babboqer, umishshum sapeq berakot lehaqel en mebarekim, vekatabti besipri haq' mqbtzyl deim yekavven bekak saggi behaki veen tzarik lemashmesh betallit qatan bishat beraka gam ledaat maran za"l, veal ken kevan shehashshikcha metzuya baadam umishtele velo mekavven lipamim, lekak nakon sheyyargil atzmo lehosip benosach leshem yichud qudesha berik hu ushekinatah hannizkar leel od debarim ellu vahareni mukan lebarek al atipat hattallit ketiqqun chakamenu zikronam libraka, vahareni mekavven liptor bibraka zo gam hattallit qatan shealay:

clarification.explanation: When one recites the blessing over the tallit, one must be careful to say "lehit'atef betzitzit" — the bet of "betzitzit" with a sheva and not a patach (that is, "be-tzitzit" and not "ba-tzitzit"). When reciting the blessing in the morning over the tallit gadol, one must have explicit intention that this blessing will also exempt the tallit katan worn under the clothes, if it was not removed at night. The reason is that there is an opinion that a separate blessing must be recited over the tallit katan in the morning, but because of the doubt, the practice is not to recite a blessing on it, relying instead on the blessing of the tallit gadol. In my book Makabtziel I wrote that this intention suffices and there is no need to touch the tallit katan at the time of the blessing, even according to Maran. Since a person may forget to have this intention, it is worthwhile to accustom oneself to add, in the wording of "for the sake of the unification," also the words: "and I am hereby prepared to recite the blessing over the wrapping of the tallit as ordained by our Sages of blessed memory, and I intend by this blessing to exempt also the tallit katan that is upon me."
takeaways: In the blessing over the tallit one says "lehit'atef betzitzit" — the bet of "betzitzit" with a sheva, not a patach.
In the morning blessing over the tallit gadol, one must explicitly intend to exempt also the tallit katan that was not removed at night.
It is recommended to add, in the wording of "for the sake of the unification," the explicit intention to exempt the tallit katan, so as not to forget.

paragraphs: Qodem sheyyebarek yeayyen veyibdoq bechute hatztzitzit shello yihyeh bahem chesron happosel, vegam yaprid hatztzitziyyot beyadayv shello yihyu hachutin mesubbakin zb"z, veraq beshabbat lo yaprid ella yibdeqem bilbad, vegam od yizzaher bekol yom libdoq uleayyen hachutim lemala baqqeren bimqom hanneqeb, sheim nipsaq sham apillu chut echad pasul, ubishat haddechaq sheicher labo o shehatztzibbur mamtinin alayv laasot petichat hahekol o liqro battora yukal lismok achazaqa velo yibdoq beotah happaam, veken mi sheholek badderek veen beyado letaqqen, katebu haacharonim sheyyesh lismok al hachazaqa velo yibdoq:

clarification.explanation: Before reciting the blessing over the tzitzit, one must check the threads and make sure there is no flaw that invalidates the tzitzit. In addition, one should separate the threads by hand so that they are not tangled with one another. On Shabbat it is forbidden to separate the threads — one only checks them. Likewise, every day one must pay special attention to the upper part of the threads, at the place where they emerge from the hole in the garment — if even one thread is torn there, the tzitzit are invalid. In a case of pressing need, such as delaying the congregation at the synagogue or the congregation waiting for him to open the ark or read from the Torah, he may rely on the presumption that the tzitzit are fit and not check them on that occasion. Also one who is traveling on the road and has no possibility of repairing the tzitzit if he finds a flaw in them — the later authorities wrote that he may rely on the presumption and not check.
takeaways: Before the blessing one checks the tzitzit threads and separates them, except on Shabbat, when one only checks and does not separate.
One checks especially the threads near the hole — one invalid thread there invalidates the entire tzitzit.
In a case of pressing need, or when there is no possibility of repair, one may rely on the presumption and not check.

paragraphs: Gam tallit qatan yizzaher lebadeqo qodem, ubazeh tihyeh gam ishto mesayyaat bammitzva shettihyeh zehira libdoq tallit qatan beet shemmazmenet habbegadim lebalah lehachalipam, vetizzaher gam ken lehaprid hachutin ki mechamat kibbus vadday yihyu mesubbakim zeh bazeh, veaz tittol sakar bazo hammitzva lehatztzil baalah min haissur, shellipamim haish bahul lilbosh begadayv veeno bodeq, ak im kol zeh hu lo yismok al ishto ella yibdoq veachar kak yebarek:

clarification.explanation: Regarding the tallit katan as well, one must be careful to check it before putting it on. The wife can assist in this mitzvah when she prepares clean garments for her husband to change into; she should check the tallit katan and separate the tzitzit, since laundering causes them to become tangled with one another. In doing so she earns great reward for having saved her husband from transgression, since sometimes the man is in a hurry to dress and forgets to check. Despite the wife's important help, the husband must not rely on her blindly, but must check the tallit himself and only then recite the blessing.
takeaways: The wife should check and separate the tzitzit of the tallit katan when preparing her husband's garments, in order to save him from transgression.
The husband must check the tallit himself before dressing and not rely solely on his wife's check, and only then recite the blessing.

paragraphs: Seder atipat hattallit gadol hu kak, achar siyyum habberaka taatop bo roshka bilbad, velo keotam hammitchakkemim leattep bo kol gupam mittechilla deen lanu ella dibre rabbenu haari"y za"l, veachar sheatepat bo roshka yihyu haarba kenapot yoredin al hakketepayim letzad panim, shenayim al tzad yamin, ushenayim al tzad semol, az tochaz techilla bishnayim shelletzad yamin vetashlikem laachoreka letzad semol, sheyyihyu kerukim sebib tzavverik al katep hassemali leachor ushettayim hassemaliyyim yishshaaru teluyim neged paneka, vetamtin meat shiur mahalak arba ummot o pachot meat, vetachazor vetashlik otam hashshenayim hassemaliyyim gam ken laachoreka letzad semol, beopen sheatta naasu kol haarba kenapot teluyim laachoreka beyachad betzad semol, vetamtin shiur mahalak arba ammot veaz torid hattallit hakkaruk betzavvarka al kol gupeka, veatta tihyeh meuttap bo roshka vegupeka beyachad, ken meporash beseper hakkavvanot derush hatztzitzit pereq ' ukemo sheddiqdeq yapeh harab "emet leyaaqob" za"l dap q"z ammud d' veken meporash lehedya besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, umah shekkatabti sheyyishheh ben hashlakat shettayim hayyemaniyyim lehashlakat shettayim hassemaliyyim shiur hilluk arba ammot, zeh lo nitparesh lehedya bedibre rabbenu za"l ubidbar harasha"sh za"l, ak hoil venitparesh sham shetztzarik lekavven bazeh kavvanot bipne atzman, ubazeh kavvanot bipne atzman dehashlakat hashtayim techilla beod shehashshettayim hassemalim odam teluyim letzad panim yesh bazeh inyan bipne atzmo, vaanachnu en anachnu mekavvenim bekavvanot haellu, lekak day lanu shennishheh hilluk arba ammot, kede leqayyem hahoraa shel maaseh zo, ukemo shekkatub: "eder eder lebaddo verivvach tasimu ben eder uben eder":

clarification.explanation: The order of wrapping the tallit is as follows: after reciting the blessing, one should place the tallit on the head alone, and not immediately wrap the whole body as some people do, but rather follow only the words of the Ari. After placing the tallit on the head, the four corners hang down over the shoulders toward the front — two on the right side and two on the left side. In the first stage, one takes the two corners on the right side and throws them backward to the left side, so that they wind around the neck and reach the left shoulder from behind, while the two left corners remain hanging in front of the face. One should wait a short time, the time it takes to walk four cubits (or a bit less), and then throw the two left corners as well backward to the left side. Now all four corners hang together behind, on the left side. One waits again the time it takes to walk four cubits, and then lowers the tallit from the neck so that it wraps both the head and the entire body together. The pause between throwing the right corners and the left corners is required in order to fulfill the order of the separate act, even though one does not have in mind the special kavanot mentioned in the books.
takeaways: After the blessing, one places the tallit on the head alone, and does not immediately wrap the entire body.

One performs the wrapping in stages, waiting the time it takes to walk four cubits between throwing the right corners and throwing the left corners; and after all four hang behind, one waits again the time it takes to walk four cubits, and only then lowers the tallit to wrap the whole body.

paragraphs: Ben betallit gadol uben betallit qatan yebarek meummad, uminhag rabbenu haari"y za"l sheggam tallit qatan haya techilla meattep bo rosho, veaach"k morid oto al gupo, ulepikak haya mebarek al tallit qatan lehitattep, vekol adam im yaaseh ken hinneh mah tob, ak mi sheeno meattep bo rosho ella tekep morido al gupo velobesho, yebarek al mitzvat tzitzit velo yebarek lehitattep:

clarification.explanation: Both for the tallit gadol and for the tallit katan, the blessing is recited while standing. The custom of the Ari was that also with the tallit katan he would first wrap it around his head and only afterward lower it onto his body, and therefore he would recite over it the blessing "lehit'atef" just as with the tallit gadol. And so it is fitting for every person to do. But one who does not wrap his head in it, but immediately lowers it onto his body and puts it on, should recite the blessing "al mitzvat tzitzit" and not "lehit'atef."
takeaways: The blessing over the tzitzit is recited while standing.
One who follows the practice of also wrapping the head with the tallit katan (like the Ari) recites "lehit'atef"; otherwise, one recites "al mitzvat tzitzit."

paragraphs: Hallobesh tallit chadash yebarek shehecheyanu achar birkat lehitattep, vetallit qatan en mebarekin shehecheyanu deen derek laasoto middabar chashub sheyyihyeh sameach bo, veim asao middabar chashub shehu sameach bo yebarek shehecheyanu:

clarification.explanation: One who wears a new tallit gadol recites Shehecheyanu after the blessing "lehit'atef." But over a tallit katan one does not recite Shehecheyanu, because it is not customary to make it from significant material that would cause joy; however, if it was made from significant material and he is glad about it, he recites Shehecheyanu.
takeaways: A new tallit gadol — one recites Shehecheyanu; a tallit katan — only if it is significant and gladdening.

paragraphs: En lehaqpid lehannicha siman betallit lasim tamid tzad echad shel hattallit al harosh velo yehapek, kemo sheyyesh nohagim lehaqpid bekak velaasot siman, ki meporash bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l deen lehaqpid al kak veyilbosh kaasher yizdammen lo:

clarification.explanation: One need not be particular about always placing the same side of the tallit on the head without turning it, as some people are accustomed to be careful about this and make a mark for it, since it is explicitly stated in the words of the Ari that one need not be particular about this, and he should wear it as it happens to come.
takeaways: There is no obligation to always place the same side of the tallit on the head — it may be switched.

paragraphs: Yizzaher shello yasir hattallit qatan mealayv beshum zeman, hen beet shena. hen beet tashmish hammitta, veraq kesheyyikkanes lammerchatz yesirennu. veim niknas lebet hakkisse veen alayv beged elyon hamkasseh et tallit qatan, az yekasseh veyatznia hatztzitziyyot shebbo shello yihyu teluyim lehedya begilluy:

clarification.explanation: One should be careful never to remove the tallit katan, neither during sleep nor during marital relations, and only when entering the bathhouse should he remove it. And if he enters a bathroom and has no outer garment covering the tallit katan, he should cover and conceal the tzitzit so that they are not left hanging in plain view.
takeaways: One wears the tallit katan at all times (even while sleeping), except in the bathhouse.
In the bathroom, one conceals the tzitzit when there is no garment covering them.

paragraphs: Im pashat tallit gadol kede likkanes lebet hakkisse, o bishbil eseq acher al daat lachazor ulelabesho miyyad, en tzarik lebarek alayv shenit veap al gab demaran za"l sebira lah lebarek, qy"l sapeq berakot lehaqel vaapillu neged sebarat maran za"l, veken hu haddin betallit qatan im posheto lehikkanes litbila lo yebarek keshellobesho beet sheyyetze, mishshum sapeq berakot veap al gab dimporash beseper hakkavvanot derabbenu haari"y za"l haya minhago lebarek al tallit qatan achar tebila, veen omerim sapeq berakot keneged rabbenu haari"y za"l, mikkol maqom yesh lomar shane rabbenu haari"y za"l shehaya mitakkeb battebila veoseh bah kavvanot harbeh, venaasa hessach daat tepe, mihu im posheto kede likkanes lammerchatz deshoheh sham harbeh yesh lebarek al pi minhag haari"y za"l. kak haaleti besipri haq' mqbtzl, mihu im hechelip begadayv velobesh tallit qatan acher, apillu shehu lobesho tekep umiyyad achar sheppashat harishon yebarek al zeh hachodesh, veken hu haddin betallit gadol im poshet zeh shealayv velobesh tallit gadol acher yebarek al hashsheni: ubesipre haq' rab pealim katabti bitshuba besiyyata dishmayya, bemi sheddarko lilbosh tzitzit utepillin bekol yom bebeto, kede sheyyikkanes lebet hakkeneset betzitzit utepillin, ak mechamat sheholek bimboot sheshsham oberim veshabim bene adam harbeh bene berit veenam bene berit, eno lobesh tallit gadol sheyyesh lo bebet hakkeneset ki nikkar leene bene adam, ella yesh lo tallit daq meod sheyyesh bo shiur tallit gadol ak eno gadol harbeh velobesho babbayit tachat haggelima shello, ulerob daqquto vegam eno arok harbeh eno nikkar leene bene adam haoberim veshabim, ukesheyyabo lebet hakkeneset yishshaer zeh alayv tachat gelimato, velobesh tallit haggadol sheyyesh lo, vehaaleti besiyyata dishmayya deyakol lebarek bebet hakkeneset al tallit hashsheni, ap al pi sheadayin harishon alayv shebberek alayv bebeto, kevan deikka hepseq mibbeto lebet hakkeneset, vegam ikka hessach haddaat shehu omer pesuqim al hammezuza, veod shoheh harbeh bederek hilluko, vesham bebet hakkeneset lobesh tallit acher gadol karauy baatipat harosh vehaggup, vehattallit shealayv hu munnach al ketepayv tachat raglayv, veod tziddadti teamim acherim bedabar zeh lebarek, veen lachush bazeh mishshum sapeq berakot:

clarification.explanation: One who removes a tallit gadol in order to enter a bathroom, or for some other purpose, intending to put it back on immediately — need not recite the blessing again (doubt regarding blessings is resolved leniently, even against the opinion of Maran); and likewise with a tallit katan removed for immersion — one does not recite the blessing when putting it back on, even though Sefer HaKavanot records that the custom of the Ari was to recite the blessing over the tallit katan after immersion (because for him there was a long diversion of the mind due to the many kavanot in the immersion, which is not the case for other people). But one who removes it to enter the bathhouse and stays there a long time — one should recite the blessing, following the custom of the Ari. And if he changed his clothes and put on a different tallit katan (or a different tallit gadol) — he recites the blessing over the new one, even though he put it on immediately after the first one. Rabbi Yosef Chaim also brought, in his responsa Rav Pe'alim, an interesting case: one who is accustomed to wear tzitzit and tefillin at home every day in order to enter the synagogue wearing them, but because he walks through alleyways with many passersby (Jews and non-Jews), he does not wear there his conspicuous tallit gadol, but rather a very thin tallit (the size of a tallit gadol, but not long) that is not noticeable under his cloak — and when he reaches the synagogue, this one remains under it, and he puts on, over it, his usual large tallit. The Ben Ish Chai ruled that he may recite the blessing in the synagogue over the second tallit, even though the first one (over which he already recited a blessing at home) is still on him — because there is an interruption between the house and the synagogue, and there is a diversion of the mind (reciting verses over the mezuzah on his way out, and a long walk along the way), and in the synagogue he wraps himself properly (head and body) in the second tallit, which rests on his shoulders over the first one that is under his clothes — and there is no concern here of a doubt regarding blessings.
takeaways: A temporary removal with immediate return (bathroom/immersion) — one does not recite the blessing again; a long stay (bathhouse) or a change to a different garment — one does recite the blessing.

One who wears a thin, concealed tallit at home for reasons of modesty or caution, and in the synagogue puts on a regular tallit gadol over it — may recite the blessing over the second one (there is an interruption and a diversion of the mind from the walk).
